topics.topic: Define size as logical hash-input length versus cumulative physical I/O
questions: Does “number of bytes that were read” mean the length of the single logical byte sequence supplied to the hash, or total physical I/O including retries, duplicate reads, and seeks?

Does `size` mean the length of the logical file-content sequence supplied to the hash, or the cumulative number of bytes transferred by every read, including retries, overlapping reads, and decoder rereads?
Is size the length of the logical byte sequence supplied to the hash, or the cumulative number of bytes fetched from the file when buffering, retries, overlapping reads, or multiple passes occur?

quotes:

topics.topic: Define size for files rejected after a partial read and its relationship to hash input
questions: What is `size` when a file is rejected after some, but not all, bytes have been read?

For a file rejected after some or all bytes were read, does the size/hash correspondence still require computing and discarding a digest, or is `size` merely a count of bytes read with no defined hash input?

quotes:
`size`
is the number of bytes that were read, the bytes `source_id` is the hash of; a file rejected before its
bytes were read has the size its metadata gave when it was listed. `source_id` is present for `ready`, `placed` and
`published` and absent for `rejected`, `reason` is present only for `rejected`, `file_ref` for `placed`
and `published`, and `photo_id` only for `published`.
judgement.why: After a partial read size is the number of bytes read; only a rejection before any bytes are read uses listed metadata, and every rejected observation omits source_id.

topics.topic: Define observation behavior when a file mutates during reading
questions: What content does an observation represent when the file changes while its bytes are being read, and must the deliverer accept the resulting stream, retry for a stable snapshot, or reject it?

quotes:
What one scan saw for one file of the photo folder. A placed file adds its `file_ref`, a published
file adds its Portal `photo_id`, and files with the same content carry the same `source_id`. The
deliverer computes it on each scan; the calling flow reads it.

Syncthing may change the folder during a scan, so a scan is not a view of one instant. Each rule applies
to what its step finds when it runs, and the next scan sees the folder as it then stands.

A scan gives each regular file of the photo folder exactly one status. The first rule that
applies decides:

| 4 | it grew past the source limit while being read | `rejected` | `too_large` |
| 5 | opening or reading it fails, which includes a file that disappeared and a path that became a symbolic link after the listing | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
judgement.divergence: One implementation reports the successfully read mixed byte stream as ready and hashes that stream, while another detects the concurrent mutation and retries to report a stable later stream; the calling flow observes different source_id values and possibly different size or status.
judgement.why: The texts permit the folder to change during a scan but do not decide whether a successful read spanning a mutation is accepted or retried for stability.

witness.initial: A regular file in the photo folder is eligible for scanning and contains content A.
events: The calling flow asks the deliverer to scan the project folder.
The deliverer begins reading the file.
Syncthing changes part of the file to content B while the read is in progress.
The deliverer completes the read without an I/O failure or crossing the source limit.
outcomes: The scan reports a ready observation whose source_id hashes the mixed stream read across the mutation.
The scan retries after detecting the mutation and reports a ready observation whose source_id hashes the stable later content B.

topics.topic: Define refusal-reason precedence when size-limit crossing and read failure both occur
questions: If reading both crosses the size limit and then fails, which refusal reason takes precedence: `too_large` or `unreadable_file`?

quotes:
A scan gives each regular file of the photo folder exactly one status. The first rule that
applies decides:

| 4 | it grew past the source limit while being read | `rejected` | `too_large` |
| 5 | opening or reading it fails, which includes a file that disappeared and a path that became a symbolic link after the listing | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
judgement.why: The first applicable rule decides, and growth past the limit is order 4 before the order-5 read failure, so the reason is too_large.
